To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) Andorra is located at a climatic transition area between Mediterranean and Atlantic climate.
1) The snow climatic zones of Andorra are characterized by a strong influence of synoptic circulation types.

1) the snow climates of Andorra are characterized by the synoptic circulation types that generate the snowfalls, 2) the different snow climates generate a spatial variability of avalanche activity that can be related to different avalanche activity scenarios, 3) the avalanche activity scenarios are related to the different snow climate patterns and 4) the different avalanche activity scenarios can be used to help the decision making and risk assessment when avalanche triggering is required
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis and interpretation of long time series of nivometeorologic data and avalanche situation.

a) the characterization of snow climate zones in Andorra, b) the characterization of different avalanche scenarios and c) the definition of a methodology to be used for the snow climate zoning of any other mountain range.

the characterization and evaluation of the snow climatic zones of Andorra, the definition of the avalanche activity scenarios related with them and the definition of the most adequate artificial avalanche triggering strategies in the different zones.

the snow climatic zones and the corresponding avalanche activity scenarios are the result of the complex interactions between the synoptic circulation types with the orography and the local meteorological conditions.
the snow climatic zones of Andorra are related with different avalanche activity scenarios.
the different snow climatic zones in Andorra are characterized by the different spatial patterns of the different synoptic circulation types.

the different circulation types generate a different spatial pattern of snow accumulation and consequently a different avalanche risk.
